# R06 IsOS dependent stop cases

[中文](README_cn.md) · [Owner contract](../../../../../docs/isos/interfaces/cores/dependent-stop.md) · [Design](../../../../../docs/isos/design/server.md)

**Design-only inventory.** `cases.json` freezes 57 expected outcomes for stub and real-owner implementation tests. `python3 tests/fixtures/dependent_stop/check_cases.py` checks shape and safety-sensitive expectations; it does not run a process or prove a physical stop. The implementation must bind the approved EOS terminal receipt to the selected child, run ID and observed PID. The `eos_receipt` tokens in this fixture are test scenarios, not EOS wire fields. `eos_receipt_confirmed.json` and `eos_receipt_unknown.json` freeze the approved EOS schema-1 `eos_terminal_stop` stdout frames; `receipt_mutation` names derive negative parser inputs from the confirmed frame.

Replay clean and negative cases through one fresh `ISOS_HOME`: direct CLI, HTTP and owner socket Stop, attached Ctrl+C, Restart/rollback, provider crash, manager shutdown, event rotation and failure. Capture process-group members and the actual EOS/MuJoCo child/socket before and after; compare run IDs and grants without printing grant values. Preserve complete output under ignored `logs/test/<run-id>/`. Unknown stop must block a new candidate and cannot become `deployment_stopped` because a PID disappeared. The final real-owner replay requires EOS and the pinned MuJoCo `0.1.1` package in both scenes; the stub may test ordering but cannot close the R06 gate.

The review cases require a leader that exits before Stop but remains unreaped for a safe original-group signal, and a deterministic leader-reap/PGID-reuse race with **no** signal to the reused group, KILL beginning at `deadline - 2,000 ms`, bounded reap and publication, durable unknown intent before signaling, crash recovery from that intent, and an atomic new-run reset after P07 publication but before spawn. Stalled intent rename and parent fsync must leave only unknown on disk even if they finish after the caller receives unknown. A live confirmed response degrades to unknown after manager restart; historical `deployment_stopped` is no safety authority. At deadline equality, the live fence publishes unknown. No late worker may publish confirmed.

The receipt cases require IsOS to read only the selected EOS raw stdout pipe before P06 normalization, bind run/PID/revision/backend/selected parts, reject duplicate or unknown keys and partial/oversized/second/late lines, and ignore other process pipes, and require EOS zero exit and both process groups drained. `managed-stop-v1` is only a preflight support announcement. EOS has a 15-second shutdown bound; IsOS defaults to a 20-second EOS grace inside 30 seconds overall. The fixture checker validates fixture shape and expected outcomes, while implementation tests must inject real raw bytes and timing.

Reason precedence is frozen: a wrong run ID on the selected EOS pipe is `eos_receipt_invalid`; a receipt only on another pipe leaves the selected receipt `eos_receipt_missing`. While the result is pending, the global deadline at or after its boundary yields `stop_deadline_exceeded` before EOS-grace or parser reasons. A late receipt strictly before the global deadline yields `eos_receipt_late`; an already published result never changes.
